name: Massachusetts Institute of Technology (MIT)
description: Private research university in Cambridge, Massachusetts, founded in 1861, world-renowned for science, engineering, and technology.

facts.about: MIT's mission is to advance knowledge and educate students in science, technology, and other areas of scholarship that will best serve the world. It is organized around five Schools plus the Schwarzman College of Computing and is known for a hands-on, problem-solving culture ('mens et manus').
facts.research_summary: Artificial intelligence and computing (CSAIL), robotics, energy and climate, biotechnology and life sciences, materials science, aerospace, nuclear science, economics, and the Media Lab for digital technology and design.

name: Harvard University
description: Private Ivy League research university in Cambridge, Massachusetts, founded in 1636, the oldest institution of higher education in the US.

facts.about: Harvard is a global leader in liberal arts education and research, comprising Harvard College and twelve graduate and professional schools. Its mission emphasizes educating citizens and citizen-leaders through transformative teaching and research.
facts.research_summary: Medicine and public health, law, business and economics, government and policy, life sciences, engineering and applied sciences, humanities, and data science.

name: Stanford University
description: Private research university in Stanford, California, founded in 1885, closely tied to Silicon Valley innovation.

facts.about: Stanford's mission is to educate future leaders and promote interdisciplinary teaching and research across the humanities, sciences, engineering, and professional fields, with a strong culture of entrepreneurship.
facts.research_summary: Artificial intelligence (HAI), computer science, bioengineering, medicine, energy and sustainability (Doerr School), business innovation, and law and policy.

name: Columbia University
description: Private Ivy League research university in New York City, founded in 1754, one of the oldest institutions of higher education in the US.

facts.about: Columbia combines a core liberal arts curriculum with extensive graduate and professional education, leveraging its New York City location for global engagement in journalism, business, law, and international affairs.
facts.research_summary: Climate and earth science (Lamont-Doherty), journalism, international and public affairs (SIPA), biomedical research, data science, and nanoscience.

name: Princeton University
description: Private Ivy League research university in Princeton, New Jersey, founded in 1746, known for undergraduate teaching and research.
programs: Arts and Sciences (Humanities, Natural Sciences, Social Sciences)

facts.about: Princeton emphasizes undergraduate liberal arts education alongside graduate research, with no medical, law, or business school, and a strong tradition of independent senior thesis work.
facts.research_summary: Physics and astrophysics (Plasma Physics Lab), public policy (Woodrow Wilson School/SPIA), economics, computer science, molecular biology, and engineering.

name: Cornell University
description: Private Ivy League land-grant research university in Ithaca, New York, founded in 1865.

facts.about: Cornell is known for its 'any person, any study' philosophy, combining private Ivy League colleges with statutory (land-grant) colleges, and operating a New York City campus (Cornell Tech) and a medical college.
facts.research_summary: Agriculture and life sciences, veterinary medicine, engineering, hospitality management, computing and information science, and human ecology.

name: Yale University
description: Private Ivy League research university in New Haven, Connecticut, founded in 1701.

facts.about: Yale is organized around Yale College's liberal arts curriculum and a wide array of graduate and professional schools, with a strong emphasis on the arts, humanities, and residential college life.
facts.research_summary: Humanities and law, medicine and public health, environmental studies, art and architecture, and molecular and cellular biology.

name: University of Chicago
description: Private research university in Chicago, Illinois, founded in 1890, known for rigorous academics and economics.

facts.about: UChicago is known for its rigorous Core Curriculum, a tradition of free inquiry, and pioneering contributions to economics (Chicago School), sociology, and law and economics.
facts.research_summary: Economics, physics (site of the first controlled nuclear reaction), public policy (Harris School), molecular engineering, and quantitative social science.

name: Johns Hopkins University
description: Private research university in Baltimore, Maryland, founded in 1876, recognized as the first US research university.

facts.about: Johns Hopkins pioneered the American research university model, integrating graduate research with undergraduate education, and is a global leader in biomedical research and public health.
facts.research_summary: Biomedical research and medicine, public health (Bloomberg School), international relations (SAIS), applied physics (APL), and engineering.

name: University of California, Berkeley
description: Public research university in Berkeley, California, founded in 1868, the flagship of the University of California system.

facts.about: UC Berkeley is a leading public research university known for academic excellence, public mission, and a legacy of scientific discovery, activism, and innovation.
facts.research_summary: Computer science and AI, physics (Lawrence Berkeley National Lab ties), chemistry, environmental science, economics, and public policy (Goldman School).

name: University of Pennsylvania
description: Private Ivy League research university in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania, founded in 1740 by Benjamin Franklin.

facts.about: Penn emphasizes interdisciplinary and practical education, home to the nation's first business school (Wharton) and a strong tradition in medicine, law, and the social sciences.
facts.research_summary: Business and finance (Wharton), medicine, bioengineering, nursing science, communication (Annenberg), and social policy.

name: Northwestern University
description: Private research university based in Evanston, Illinois, founded in 1851, with a campus in Chicago.
programs: Weinberg College of Arts and Sciences

facts.about: Northwestern combines strong undergraduate liberal arts with top-ranked professional schools in journalism, business, law, and engineering, emphasizing interdisciplinary collaboration.
facts.research_summary: Journalism and communication (Medill), materials science and nanotechnology, biomedical engineering, management science (Kellogg), and neuroscience.

name: Duke University
description: Private research university in Durham, North Carolina, founded in 1838, known for medicine and basketball.
programs: Trinity College of Arts and Sciences

facts.about: Duke integrates a strong undergraduate liberal arts college (Trinity) with nationally ranked graduate schools in medicine, law, business, and public policy, and an emphasis on interdisciplinary research.
facts.research_summary: Medicine and genomics (Duke Health), public policy (Sanford School), environmental science (Nicholas School), and global health.

name: University of Michigan–Ann Arbor
description: Public research university in Ann Arbor, Michigan, founded in 1817, one of the largest and oldest public universities in the US.

facts.about: Michigan is a comprehensive public research university offering an extensive range of undergraduate, graduate, and professional programs, with a strong athletics tradition and large research enterprise.
facts.research_summary: Engineering and robotics, medicine and life sciences, business (Ross), public policy (Ford School), and social research (ISR).

name: Brown University
description: Private Ivy League research university in Providence, Rhode Island, founded in 1764.

facts.about: Brown is known for its Open Curriculum, which gives undergraduates significant freedom to design their own course of study, alongside strong research programs and a medical school.
facts.research_summary: Cognitive and brain sciences, public health, international and public affairs (Watson Institute), and applied mathematics.

name: New York University (NYU)
description: Private research university based in New York City, founded in 1831, with a global network of campuses.

facts.about: NYU is one of the largest private research universities in the US, known for its urban campus integrated into New York City and a global network including campuses in Abu Dhabi and Shanghai.
facts.research_summary: Data science and AI (Courant, Center for Data Science), law, business (Stern), the arts (Tisch), and public service (Wagner).

name: Rice University
description: Private research university in Houston, Texas, founded in 1912, known for a small student body and strong STEM programs.

facts.about: Rice combines a small liberal arts college atmosphere with major research programs, emphasizing undergraduate teaching, residential colleges, and close ties to Houston's energy and medical sectors.
facts.research_summary: Nanotechnology and materials science, space science (historic NASA ties), bioengineering, and computational science.

name: University of California, Los Angeles (UCLA)
description: Public research university in Los Angeles, California, founded in 1919, part of the University of California system.

facts.about: UCLA is a major public research university known for its breadth of academic programs, athletics, film and media studies, and a large academic medical center.
facts.research_summary: Film, television and media (TFT), medicine and biosciences (David Geffen School of Medicine), engineering, and public policy.

name: Boston University
description: Private research university in Boston, Massachusetts, founded in 1839, one of the largest private universities in the US.

facts.about: BU is a large, urban research university offering a broad range of undergraduate and graduate programs across many colleges, with a strong emphasis on global studies and communication.
facts.research_summary: Infectious disease research (NEIDL), engineering, communication and journalism, and global health.

name: Georgetown University
description: Private Jesuit research university in Washington, D.C., founded in 1789, the oldest Catholic and Jesuit university in the US.

facts.about: Georgetown is known for its Jesuit values, global and international affairs programs, and proximity to the US federal government, shaping strengths in law, diplomacy, and public policy.
facts.research_summary: International affairs and diplomacy (Walsh School), law and public policy, business ethics (McDonough), and global health.

name: Washington University in St. Louis (WashU)
description: Private research university in St. Louis, Missouri, founded in 1853.

facts.about: WashU is a major research university known for strengths in medicine, biomedical engineering, business, and the arts, with a highly residential undergraduate experience.
facts.research_summary: Medicine and genomics (School of Medicine), biomedical engineering, social work (Brown School), and architecture and design.

name: Tufts University
description: Private research university based in Medford/Somerville, Massachusetts, founded in 1852.
programs: Fletcher School of Law and Diplomacy

facts.about: Tufts is a mid-sized research university known for interdisciplinary study, international relations (Fletcher School), and strong programs in medicine, dental medicine, and veterinary medicine.
facts.research_summary: International relations and diplomacy (Fletcher School), nutrition science, biomedical sciences, and engineering.

name: University of Rochester
description: Private research university in Rochester, New York, founded in 1850.

facts.about: The University of Rochester combines a research-intensive environment with a flexible undergraduate curriculum, and is home to a prominent medical center and music school.
facts.research_summary: Optics and photonics (Institute of Optics), music education (Eastman), medicine and biomedical engineering, and data science.

name: California Institute of Technology (Caltech)
description: Private research university in Pasadena, California, founded in 1891, focused exclusively on science and engineering.

facts.about: Caltech is a small, highly selective institute focused on science and engineering education and research, and manages NASA's Jet Propulsion Laboratory (JPL).
facts.research_summary: Astronomy and astrophysics (JPL, LIGO), chemistry, physics, planetary science, and computer and information science.

name: George Washington University
description: Private research university in Washington, D.C., founded in 1821.
programs: Columbian College of Arts and Sciences

facts.about: GW leverages its Washington, D.C. location for strengths in political science, international affairs, law, and public health, serving a large and diverse student body.
facts.research_summary: International affairs (Elliott School), public health, political communication, and cybersecurity policy.

name: Vanderbilt University
description: Private research university in Nashville, Tennessee, founded in 1873.

facts.about: Vanderbilt is a research university known for its strong undergraduate colleges, medical center, and education school, combining Southern heritage with a national academic reputation.
facts.research_summary: Medicine and biomedical science (Vanderbilt Medical Center), education and human development (Peabody), and engineering.

name: Emory University
description: Private research university in Atlanta, Georgia, founded in 1836.
programs: Emory College of Arts and Sciences
Nell Hodgson Woodruff School of Nursing

facts.about: Emory is known for strong programs in health sciences, business, and the liberal arts, with close ties to the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) and the Carter Center.
facts.research_summary: Public health and infectious disease (Rollins School), vaccine research, business analytics (Goizueta), and neuroscience.

name: University of Notre Dame
description: Private Catholic research university in Notre Dame, Indiana, founded in 1842.

facts.about: Notre Dame integrates Catholic intellectual tradition with rigorous liberal arts and professional education, known for strong undergraduate residential life and a prominent athletics program.
facts.research_summary: Peace studies (Kroc Institute), engineering, theology, and nanotechnology.

name: Dartmouth College
description: Private Ivy League research university in Hanover, New Hampshire, founded in 1769.
programs: Guarini School of Graduate and Advanced Studies

facts.about: Dartmouth is known for its strong undergraduate focus within an Ivy League research institution, along with graduate programs in business, medicine, engineering, and arts and sciences.
facts.research_summary: Health policy and clinical practice (Dartmouth Institute), computer science, and engineering (Thayer School).

name: Northeastern University
description: Private research university in Boston, Massachusetts, founded in 1898, known for cooperative education (co-op).
programs: College of Arts Media and Design

facts.about: Northeastern is distinguished by its experiential learning model, particularly its co-op program integrating academic study with professional work experience, and operates a global network of campuses.
facts.research_summary: Cybersecurity, health sciences, network science, and experiential and use-inspired research.

name: Boston College
description: Private Jesuit Catholic research university in Chestnut Hill, Massachusetts, founded in 1863.
programs: Morrissey College of Arts and Sciences
Lynch School of Education and Human Development

facts.about: Boston College blends Jesuit Catholic educational tradition with liberal arts and professional education, emphasizing formation of the whole person alongside academic rigor.
facts.research_summary: Theology and Catholic studies, social work (Boston College School of Social Work), and finance.

name: Case Western Reserve University
description: Private research university in Cleveland, Ohio, formed in 1967 from the merger of Case Institute of Technology and Western Reserve University.

facts.about: Case Western Reserve is a research university with strong programs in engineering, medicine, law, and management, closely linked to Cleveland's medical and cultural institutions.
facts.research_summary: Biomedical engineering, macromolecular science, medicine (Cleveland Clinic partnership), and management science.

name: Rensselaer Polytechnic Institute (RPI)
description: Private technological research university in Troy, New York, founded in 1824, the oldest technological university in the English-speaking world.

facts.about: RPI focuses on science, engineering, and technology education with an emphasis on innovation and entrepreneurship, and hosts one of the most powerful university-owned supercomputers.
facts.research_summary: Computational science (AI Research Center), biotechnology, nanotechnology, and cybersecurity.

name: Tulane University
description: Private research university in New Orleans, Louisiana, founded in 1834.

facts.about: Tulane is known for strong programs in public health, tropical medicine, and law, with an emphasis on service learning tied to its New Orleans location.
facts.research_summary: Tropical medicine and public health, disaster resilience, and coastal environmental science.

name: Brandeis University
description: Private research university in Waltham, Massachusetts, founded in 1948.
programs: Heller School for Social Policy and Management

facts.about: Brandeis is a mid-sized research university founded on Jewish values of academic and social justice, with strengths in the social sciences, life sciences, and international studies.
facts.research_summary: Neuroscience, social policy (Heller School), and Jewish studies.

name: Swarthmore College
description: Private liberal arts college in Swarthmore, Pennsylvania, founded in 1864.
programs: Engineering (one of few liberal arts colleges offering a full engineering major)

facts.about: Swarthmore is a highly selective liberal arts college known for rigorous academics, an honors program, and a Quaker-founded tradition of social responsibility.
facts.research_summary: Undergraduate research across the natural sciences, engineering, and social sciences, with strong peace and conflict studies programs.

name: Wake Forest University
description: Private research university in Winston-Salem, North Carolina, founded in 1834.

facts.about: Wake Forest combines a liberal arts college experience with graduate and professional schools in law, business, medicine, and divinity, under the motto 'Pro Humanitate'.
facts.research_summary: Regenerative medicine (Wake Forest Institute), business analytics, and law and policy.

name: University of Richmond
description: Private liberal arts university in Richmond, Virginia, founded in 1830.
programs: School of Professional and Continuing Studies

facts.about: The University of Richmond combines a liberal arts college with specialized schools in business, leadership studies, and law, emphasizing small class sizes and undergraduate research.
facts.research_summary: Leadership studies, undergraduate research fellowships across sciences and humanities.

name: Lehigh University
description: Private research university in Bethlehem, Pennsylvania, founded in 1865.
programs: P.C. Rossin College of Engineering and Applied Science

facts.about: Lehigh is known for integrating engineering, business, and the liberal arts, with strong industry partnerships and a compact, research-active campus.
facts.research_summary: Materials science, nanotechnology, and supply chain/business analytics.

name: Middlebury College
description: Private liberal arts college in Middlebury, Vermont, founded in 1800.
programs: Middlebury Institute of International Studies at Monterey

facts.about: Middlebury is known for its strength in language study and international programs, including its renowned summer Language Schools and study-abroad network, alongside a traditional liberal arts curriculum.
facts.research_summary: Environmental studies, language pedagogy, and international and global studies.

name: Williams College
description: Private liberal arts college in Williamstown, Massachusetts, founded in 1793.
programs: Divisions of Languages and the Arts
Social Studies; Williams-Mystic (maritime studies); Center for Development Economics

facts.about: Williams is a highly selective liberal arts college known for its tutorial-style teaching, small classes, and strong programs in the arts, sciences, and humanities.
facts.research_summary: Undergraduate research in the sciences, art history (Williams-Clark Art Institute program), and economics.

name: Smith College
description: Private women's liberal arts college in Northampton, Massachusetts, founded in 1871.
programs: Ada Comstock Scholars Program (for non-traditional students)

facts.about: Smith is the largest women's college in the US, offering a liberal arts curriculum with strong programs in engineering (unique among women's colleges) and the sciences.
facts.research_summary: Engineering (Picker Engineering Program), neuroscience, and the study of women and gender.

name: Villanova University
description: Private Augustinian Catholic research university in Villanova, Pennsylvania, founded in 1842.
programs: College of Liberal Arts and Sciences
M. Louise Fitzpatrick College of Nursing

facts.about: Villanova integrates Augustinian Catholic values with programs in engineering, business, nursing, and law, emphasizing community and ethical leadership.
facts.research_summary: Sustainable engineering, business analytics, and nursing/health sciences research.

name: Wesleyan University
description: Private liberal arts university in Middletown, Connecticut, founded in 1831.
programs: Liberal Arts (Humanities, Social and Natural Sciences)

facts.about: Wesleyan offers a liberal arts curriculum with unusual breadth, including a strong film studies program, and has both undergraduate and select graduate/PhD programs.
facts.research_summary: Film studies, science (with active PhD programs in molecular biology and physics), and social sciences.

name: Carleton College
description: Private liberal arts college in Northfield, Minnesota, founded in 1866.
programs: Liberal Arts (Arts and Literature, Humanities, Natural Sciences and Mathematics, Social Sciences)

facts.about: Carleton is a highly selective liberal arts college known for intellectual intensity, strong science programs, and a collaborative, non-competitive academic culture.
facts.research_summary: Geology and environmental science, mathematics, and undergraduate research across disciplines.

name: Vassar College
description: Private liberal arts college in Poughkeepsie, New York, founded in 1861, originally a women's college and now fully coeducational.
programs: Liberal Arts (Arts, Humanities, Natural Sciences, Social Sciences)

facts.about: Vassar is a highly selective liberal arts college known for its open curriculum, strong arts and humanities programs, and historic campus.
facts.research_summary: Environmental studies, art history, and interdisciplinary humanities research.

name: Amherst College
description: Private liberal arts college in Amherst, Massachusetts, founded in 1821.
programs: Five College Consortium (shared courses with UMass Amherst, Smith, Mount Holyoke, Hampshire)

facts.about: Amherst is a highly selective liberal arts college known for its open curriculum with no core requirements, small class sizes, and membership in the Five College Consortium.
facts.research_summary: Undergraduate research across the sciences and humanities, and interdisciplinary studies through the Five Colleges consortium.

name: Wellesley College
description: Private women's liberal arts college in Wellesley, Massachusetts, founded in 1870.
programs: Liberal Arts (Humanities, Social Sciences, Natural Sciences and Mathematics)

facts.about: Wellesley is a highly selective women's liberal arts college known for producing influential women leaders, with a rigorous curriculum and cross-registration with MIT.
facts.research_summary: Undergraduate research across sciences and social sciences, women's leadership studies, and economics.

name: Colby College
description: Private liberal arts college in Waterville, Maine, founded in 1813.
programs: Liberal Arts (Arts and Humanities, Natural Sciences, Social Sciences)

facts.about: Colby is a selective liberal arts college known for its rural Maine setting, environmental studies programs, and emphasis on global and experiential learning.
facts.research_summary: Environmental and climate science, marine studies, and undergraduate research fellowships.

name: Bowdoin College
description: Private liberal arts college in Brunswick, Maine, founded in 1794.
programs: Liberal Arts (Humanities, Natural Sciences, Social and Behavioral Sciences)

facts.about: Bowdoin is a highly selective liberal arts college known for its need-blind admissions, strong sense of community, and Arctic studies legacy (Peary-MacMillan Arctic Museum).
facts.research_summary: Arctic and polar studies, environmental studies, and undergraduate research in the sciences.

name: Washington and Lee University
description: Private liberal arts university in Lexington, Virginia, founded in 1749.
programs: Williams School of Commerce Economics and Politics

facts.about: Washington and Lee is a small liberal arts university with an honor system dating back generations, offering an undergraduate college and a school of law.
facts.research_summary: Undergraduate research in the sciences and humanities, and legal scholarship at the School of Law.

name: Harvey Mudd College
description: Private engineering, science, and mathematics liberal arts college in Claremont, California, founded in 1955.
programs: Humanities Social Sciences and the Arts

facts.about: Harvey Mudd is a small, highly selective STEM-focused liberal arts college requiring a strong humanities and social science component alongside technical study, part of the Claremont Colleges consortium.
facts.research_summary: Engineering, computer science, mathematics, and interdisciplinary clinic-based sponsored research projects.

name: Davidson College
description: Private liberal arts college in Davidson, North Carolina, founded in 1837.
programs: Liberal Arts (Humanities, Natural Sciences, Social Sciences)

facts.about: Davidson is a selective liberal arts college with Presbyterian roots, known for its honor code and strong pre-professional and STEM programs.
facts.research_summary: Undergraduate research in the natural sciences, and public policy through the Center for Civic Engagement.

name: Pomona College
description: Private liberal arts college in Claremont, California, founded in 1887, the founding member of the Claremont Colleges.
programs: Liberal Arts (Humanities, Natural Sciences, Social Sciences)

facts.about: Pomona is a highly selective liberal arts college offering broad access to resources of the Claremont Colleges consortium while maintaining a small, close-knit academic community.
facts.research_summary: Undergraduate research across sciences and humanities, and environmental analysis.

name: Barnard College
description: Private women's liberal arts college in New York City, founded in 1889, affiliated with Columbia University.
programs: Liberal Arts (Humanities, Natural Sciences, Social Sciences)

facts.about: Barnard is a women's liberal arts college with an affiliation agreement giving students access to Columbia University's resources while maintaining an independent faculty and curriculum.
facts.research_summary: Women's studies, urban studies, and undergraduate research in the sciences.

name: Hamilton College
description: Private liberal arts college in Clinton, New York, founded in 1793.
programs: Liberal Arts (Humanities, Natural Sciences, Social Sciences)

facts.about: Hamilton is known for its open curriculum with no distribution requirements and a strong emphasis on writing across the curriculum.
facts.research_summary: Undergraduate research in the sciences, writing and rhetoric studies.

name: Colgate University
description: Private liberal arts university in Hamilton, New York, founded in 1819.
programs: Liberal Arts (Humanities, Natural Sciences and Mathematics, Social Sciences)

facts.about: Colgate is a selective liberal arts institution offering a broad curriculum with distinctive first-year seminar requirements and strong study-abroad participation.
facts.research_summary: Undergraduate research across natural sciences and social sciences, and geology field studies.

name: Wheaton College (Massachusetts)
description: Private liberal arts college in Norton, Massachusetts, founded in 1834.
programs: Liberal Arts (Humanities, Natural Sciences, Social Sciences)

facts.about: Wheaton College (Massachusetts) is a small, coeducational liberal arts college known for its Connections curriculum linking coursework across disciplines and strong career preparation programs.
facts.research_summary: Undergraduate research opportunities across the sciences and humanities via the Wheaton Fellows programs.

name: Savannah College of Art and Design (SCAD)
description: Private art and design university with campuses in Savannah and Atlanta, Georgia, and Lacoste, France, founded in 1978.

facts.about: SCAD is one of the largest art and design universities in the US, offering career-focused degrees across a wide range of creative disciplines with strong industry partnerships.
facts.research_summary: Applied creative research in animation, game development, fashion, and industrial design (SCADpro studio).

name: Saint Joseph's University
description: Private Jesuit Catholic university in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania, founded in 1851.

facts.about: Saint Joseph's combines Jesuit Catholic education with strong business and health science programs, following a merger with University of the Sciences in 2022.
facts.research_summary: Pharmaceutical and health sciences, business analytics, and food marketing research.

name: The University of Tulsa
description: Private research university in Tulsa, Oklahoma, founded in 1894.

facts.about: The University of Tulsa is a mid-sized private research university known for its petroleum engineering and cybersecurity programs, rooted in the region's energy industry.
facts.research_summary: Petroleum engineering, cybersecurity, and energy-related geosciences.
facts.athletic_conference: NCAA Division I – American Athletic Conference

name: Grinnell College
description: Private liberal arts college in Grinnell, Iowa, founded in 1846.
programs: Liberal Arts (Humanities, Natural Sciences, Social Studies)

facts.about: Grinnell is a highly selective liberal arts college known for its open curriculum, social justice tradition, and large endowment relative to its size.
facts.research_summary: Undergraduate research (Mentored Advanced Projects) across sciences and humanities.

name: Bates College
description: Private liberal arts college in Lewiston, Maine, founded in 1855.
programs: Liberal Arts (Humanities, Natural Sciences, Social Sciences)

facts.about: Bates is a selective liberal arts college with an early history of coeducation and abolitionist roots, known for its short-term (winter) academic term.
facts.research_summary: Undergraduate thesis-based research across disciplines, environmental and coastal studies.

name: Gonzaga University
description: Private Jesuit Catholic university in Spokane, Washington, founded in 1887.

facts.about: Gonzaga is a Jesuit Catholic university known for its liberal arts core curriculum, engineering and business programs, and nationally prominent basketball program.
facts.research_summary: Engineering and applied science, business ethics, and Catholic social teaching studies.
facts.athletic_conference: NCAA Division I – West Coast Conference

name: Rhode Island School of Design (RISD)
description: Private art and design college in Providence, Rhode Island, founded in 1877.

facts.about: RISD is one of the most prestigious art and design colleges in the US, offering studio-intensive undergraduate and graduate programs alongside a liberal arts curriculum.
facts.research_summary: Design research and innovation, materials and textiles research, and studio-based creative practice.

name: Haverford College
description: Private liberal arts college in Haverford, Pennsylvania, founded in 1833 with Quaker roots.
programs: Liberal Arts (Humanities, Natural Sciences, Social Sciences)

facts.about: Haverford is a small, highly selective liberal arts college known for its honor code, Quaker heritage, and close partnership with Bryn Mawr College.
facts.research_summary: Undergraduate research and senior thesis work across sciences and humanities.

name: Trinity University
description: Private liberal arts university in San Antonio, Texas, founded in 1869.

facts.about: Trinity University combines liberal arts education with select professional programs including engineering science and business, emphasizing undergraduate research.
facts.research_summary: Undergraduate research across sciences and engineering, and geosciences fieldwork.
facts.athletic_conference: NCAA Division III – Southern Collegiate Athletic Conference

name: College of the Holy Cross
description: Private Jesuit Catholic liberal arts college in Worcester, Massachusetts, founded in 1843.
programs: Liberal Arts (Humanities, Natural and Mathematical Sciences, Social Sciences)

facts.about: Holy Cross is a highly selective Jesuit liberal arts college focused exclusively on undergraduate education, with a strong core curriculum and emphasis on service.
facts.research_summary: Undergraduate research across sciences and humanities, Jesuit-inspired social justice scholarship.

name: Bentley University
description: Private business-focused university in Waltham, Massachusetts, founded in 1917.
programs: Business (Accountancy, Finance, Marketing, Management, Information Design and Corporate Communication)

facts.about: Bentley integrates business education with arts and sciences, emphasizing analytics, technology, and ethics in business practice.
facts.research_summary: Business analytics, cybersecurity, and corporate ethics research (Hoffman Center).

name: Colorado College
description: Private liberal arts college in Colorado Springs, Colorado, founded in 1874.
programs: Liberal Arts (Humanities, Natural Sciences, Social Sciences)

facts.about: Colorado College is known for its Block Plan, where students take one course at a time in intensive three-and-a-half week blocks, alongside a traditional liberal arts curriculum.
facts.research_summary: Undergraduate research in environmental science, geology, and southwestern studies.
facts.athletic_conference: NCAA Division III – Southern Collegiate Athletic Conference

name: Pratt Institute
description: Private art, design, and architecture institute in Brooklyn, New York, founded in 1887.

facts.about: Pratt Institute is known for professional programs in art, design, architecture, and information science, with a strong studio-based curriculum.
facts.research_summary: Design research, sustainable architecture, and library and information science studies.

name: Macalester College
description: Private liberal arts college in Saint Paul, Minnesota, founded in 1874.
programs: Liberal Arts (Humanities, Natural Sciences and Mathematics, Social Sciences)

facts.about: Macalester is known for its emphasis on internationalism, multiculturalism, and civic engagement within a rigorous liberal arts curriculum.
facts.research_summary: Undergraduate research in international studies, environmental studies, and the sciences.
facts.athletic_conference: NCAA Division III – Minnesota Intercollegiate Athletic Conference

name: Butler University
description: Private university in Indianapolis, Indiana, founded in 1855.

facts.about: Butler is known for its strong undergraduate teaching focus, particularly in pharmacy, business, and the arts, alongside a nationally recognized basketball program.
facts.research_summary: Pharmaceutical sciences, health sciences, and business analytics.
facts.athletic_conference: NCAA Division I – Big East Conference

name: Connecticut College
description: Private liberal arts college in New London, Connecticut, founded in 1911.
programs: Liberal Arts (Humanities, Natural Sciences, Social Sciences)
Interdisciplinary Centers (International Studies, Environmental Studies, Arts Management)

facts.about: Connecticut College emphasizes interdisciplinary study and global engagement through its distinctive certificate programs alongside a traditional liberal arts major.
facts.research_summary: Undergraduate research in environmental studies, maritime studies, and the sciences.
facts.athletic_conference: NCAA Division III – New England Small College Athletic Conference

name: Loyola University Maryland
description: Private Jesuit Catholic university in Baltimore, Maryland, founded in 1852.
programs: Sellinger School of Business and Management

facts.about: Loyola University Maryland combines Jesuit liberal arts education with programs in business and education, emphasizing service and ethical leadership.
facts.research_summary: Business ethics, education policy, and undergraduate science research.

name: DePauw University
description: Private liberal arts university in Greencastle, Indiana, founded in 1837.

facts.about: DePauw is a liberal arts university known for its School of Music and strong emphasis on experiential learning, leadership, and pre-professional preparation.
facts.research_summary: Undergraduate research in the sciences and management fellows program studies.
facts.athletic_conference: NCAA Division III – North Coast Athletic Conference

name: The Juilliard School
description: Private performing arts conservatory in New York City, founded in 1905.
programs: Music (Instrumental, Vocal Arts, Jazz, Historical Performance, Composition)

facts.about: Juilliard is one of the world's leading conservatories, training students exclusively in dance, drama, and music at the highest professional level.
